  "text": "My mother arrived with a saucepan wrapped in a towel.

“You said you had nothing for lunch.”

“I said I hadn't decided.”

“Well, now you have.”

She put it on the cooker and lifted the lid. Two potatoes rolled against a piece of chicken.

“Don't heat it too much. It'll go dry.”

I reached for a plate.

“Not that one. You'll want a proper edge.”

We had bought these plates together. She had held each one up in the shop, checking the glaze.

I took a bowl instead.

While I ate, she examined the basil on the windowsill.

“This wants water.”

“It had some yesterday.”

“Did it?”

She filled a glass and poured half into the pot, then drank the rest.

“Have you eaten?” I asked.

“I had a bit while I was cooking.”

I got another bowl. She watched me divide the chicken.

“I'm not taking your lunch.”

“You brought enough for four.”

“Those potatoes needed using.”

She sat down without removing her coat. Halfway through, she unbuttoned it.

Afterwards, I washed the saucepan while she dried. The towel she'd brought was thin in the middle, with a brown mark near one corner.

“I remember this,” I said.

“You put it on the hob.”

“I was twelve.”

“You were old enough.”

She folded it over the saucepan handle and waited by the door while I found her umbrella.

“Keep the pan,” she said.

“What will you cook in?”

“I've got others.”

I handed her the umbrella. She checked the strap was fastened.

“Bring it Sunday,” she said. “I'll need it then.”"
